intro: Works out ring end gap from bore and engine use (ring manufacturers' method).

warn.never_under: Never run less than the minimum gap: when hot, the ends butt together and the ring breaks or scores the bore.
warn.over_ok: A slightly larger gap (up to +30%) has no noticeable effect on sealing.

step.s1: Clean the bore and ring; measure each ring in the cylinder it will be fitted to.
step.s2: Place the ring in the bore and square it with an upside-down piston, about 15–20 mm below the deck.
step.s3: Measure the gap with a feeler gauge: it should slide in with light drag.
step.s4: If the gap is too small, file one end only with a ring filer, from the outside in, a little at a time.
step.s5: Deburr the filed end with a fine stone so it cannot scratch the bore.
step.s6: Check again, then mark each ring with its cylinder and groove.
